C-46 (ss. 462.3-462.5); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44 (s. 15.2, individuals with significant control register); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the intended directors' and shareholders' passport/ID pages
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public or embassy legalization desk
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if home state is not a Hague party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds for initial capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depositary bank in the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization (no apostille possible for bank letters; bank officer notarization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translated copy of constitutional documents (if founder entity exists)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization + certified translation into French/English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of good standing / non-disclosure of statutes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national company registry of the ultimate parent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) guidance, the Canadian sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list for USD-denominated transactions, and the Canadian provincial securities regulators' enforcement lists; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) as defined in ss. 1-2 of the PCMLTFA regulations. The process requires ongoing automated and manual verification at onboarding, within 30 days of any material change, and at least annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online platform (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) with prior NUANS/Québec-name search through authorized service providers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the corporate name must be in French or include a French version of equal prominence; any foreign-language name requires a French transliteration/translation or a secured French name. In Quebec, names are entered in the French alphabet and transliteration from non-Latin scripts is mandatory; the legal name is the French form for public registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If REQ rejects the proposed name, submit a written reconsideration request within 30 days of the rejection notice, via the REQ portal or registered mail, referencing the NUANS file number and legal arguments; if the reconsideration is denied, institute an administrative appeal before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) under the Code of Civil Procedure and the Administrative Justice Act (CQLR c. J-3) within 60 days of the denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk vertical cloud software company, provided the address is a physical street location in Quebec at which legal process can be served and representative documents are available; dedicated virtual office arrangements are acceptable if they satisfy the REQ 'place of business' standard; mail-only/p.o. box addresses are not acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% annual likelihood) for the specified ISIC 6201 cloud-software vertical; unannounced inspections are unlikely absent regulatory red flags, but REQ may require production of books/records and may verify commercial substance if a passive or shell-like pattern is detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized NUANS search provider (via REQ portal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff/third-party fee set by the provider; typical CAD $40-55

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of incorporation filing and government registration duty
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed administrative fee under the Regulation respecting the fees payable for the communication of information and services provided by the registrar (approx CAD $360)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and statutory records custodianship (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / virtual office service provider in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Private market rate; competitive benchmark CAD 200-300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, certified translations and apostille/consular legalization bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, certified translator, and/or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimate based on notary tariff and consular fee schedule, depending on country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Standard legal due diligence package (name clearance, UBO/AML assessment, drafting memorandum and articles)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate; fixed fee for low-risk simple corporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA), particularly sections 50-55 (incorporation), 105-128 (share issuance), 135-143 (registered office), 155-156 (director eligibility), and 214 (no minimum paid-up capital)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Corporate Registry Branch, Direction générale de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed under section 51 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: QBCA imposes no minimum paid-up capital or authorized capital requirement; no escrow account or bank certificate is mandatory. A corporation may be incorporated without issued shares. Initial shares may be subscribed for nominal consideration and issued for money, property, or past services, as authorized by the board in the first resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: (1) The share subscription agreements and the share allocation table annexed as Exhibit A are approved, and the Board authorizes the issuance of common shares to each subscriber against the contribution of the agreed subscription price, and the execution and delivery of share certificates. (2) The registered office of the Corporation is established at the address approved by the directors in accordance with section 223 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act. (3) The individuals whose names are set out in the officer appointment schedule shall be, and they are hereby, appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, respectively. The officers shall serve until successors are appointed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Availability Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REDE), Name Reservation and Declaration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REDE online portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) or file a paper 'Réservation de nom' form. Verify that the proposed name complies with the Quebec Business Corporations Act name regulations and, where applicable, with the Charter of the French Language (approval of the Office québécois de la langue française for a commercial designation other than French). Provide up to three alternate names. Obtain a name reservation certificate valid for 90 days to attach to the subsequent Articles of Incorporation. For a numbered company, request a corporate designation number instead.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form
Proposed corporate name (French compulsory commercial designation where applicable)
OQLF approval certificate if relying on an exemption
Identification and address of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the registry states the legal grounds; the applicant may file revised name choices, appeal the refusal in writing to the Director of Compliance, or proceed as a numbered company under the QBCA to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation with the Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Corporate Registry Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed 'Statuts de constitution' electronically via REDE's secure online filing portal or by paper where more than 20 incorporators are involved. The articles must state the corporate name or designated number, share classes and maximum number of shares, restrictions on share transfers if any, number of directors, any restrictions on business, and the municipal registered office location. Pay the indexed statutory registration fee (approximately CAD 322, subject to annual revision) by credit card or account debit. Once the registry processes the articles, it issues a Certificate of Incorporation and assigns a Quebec Entreprise Number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Completed articles of incorporation signed and dated by each incorporator
Corporate name reservation certificate (if not a numbered company)
Proof of payment of registration fee
Consent of initial directors to act as directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an information query or inspection notice, the representatives may submit amended articles within 45 days or, if accepted, no further action is needed. Where application is deemed abandoned, a new filing may be made on the corrected form without prejudice; payment corrections will cure fee discrepancies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Organization and Initial Board Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the certificate of incorporation, the sole or plurality of directors execute the first board resolution covering approval of share subscriptions, issuance of share certificates, establishment of the registered office address, appointment of officers, adoption of by-laws, approval of corporate seal, and opening of a corporate bank account. Minutes and unanimous consents must be entered into the corporate records book and signed by the directors. If only one director exists, the sole director may pass the resolutions by written consent in lieu of a meeting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Initial consent of directors
Share subscription ledger or share allocation schedule
Officer appointment schedule
Corporate records book and bank account mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No external filing is required for internal governance; any omission is cured by adopting a corrective resolution in the minute book. Retroactive resolutions are valid in ordinary course and ratified by subsequent board action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec and Federal Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Registre des entreprises) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On incorporation, REDE automatically assigns the Quebec Entreprise Number (NEQ). The company must open the necessary Revenu Québec accounts for QST registration, employer source deductions, and the Health Services Fund via forms or the SOAR/Account Management service. Register separately with the CRA for GST/HST using Form RC1, or rely on the combined Quebec/Federal program when eligible. For a cloud software subscription business, register if taxable sales exceed CAD 30,000 per year or if annual payroll triggers source deductions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Quebec Entreprise Number (NEQ) assigned by REDE
Identification and residence of all directors
Estimated first-year revenue and payroll information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If accounts are incomplete or not opened on a timely basis, the taxpayer may file a voluntary disclosure with Revenu Québec or CRA and request penalty waiver; retroactive registration is permitted to the date the liability arose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) and the competent municipal permit office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after the first employee is hired, the employer must open a CNESST occupational health and safety account and submit a registration request. For the leased office or light-industrial space, obtain a municipal occupancy permit (permis d'occupation) or building inspection certificate from the local borough or municipal permit office. Arrange a fire prevention inspection per the Quebec Fire Safety Regulation and provide floor plans and lease documentation. For a standard software cloud office, no environmental impact assessment is required; the representative confirms zoning and fire-code conformity on site.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Copy of signed commercial lease
Floor plan and description of premises
Fire safety compliance certificate
CNESST registration request
Municipal occupancy permit application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late CNESST registration can be remedied by filing a late application with an administrative penalty; a municipal occupancy permit may be issued retroactively if the premises comply; an adverse fire inspection may be cured by performing the required corrective actions and obtaining a conditional occupancy permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MÉIE), Direction générale de la transformation numérique et de l'innovation, in coordination with municipal building inspection and fire safety authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Operating and Occupancy Permit (Permis d'occupation) for a Cloud Software and Professional Service Office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category I (low-impact service activity). No mandatory environmental impact assessment is required under the Quebec Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) and the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment for an ERP/CRM cloud software provider.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations produce no industrial wastewater discharge, no relevant VOCs in quantities approaching regulated thresholds, and no hazardous waste. Sanitary discharge must comply with municipal sewer by-laws and Quebec's Regulation respecting municipal wastewater works, generally pH 6.0 to 9.5 and BOD5 below the municipal limit. Electronic waste and used IT equipment must be managed under the Quebec Regulation respecting the recovery and value recovery of residual materials and relevant electronic products stewardship plans. For any back-up generators, operational noise and fugitive emissions must respect the municipal noise by-law and CNESST occupational exposure limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification requires an evacuation plan, portable extinguishers, emergency lighting, alarm testing, and annual inspection by the local fire prevention service. Structural clearance, where server racks or high-density storage are installed, requires an engineer's load assessment in conformity with Chapter I of the Quebec Construction Code. Workplace clearance is obtained via CNESST verifying electrical safety, workspace ergonomics, assembly of first-aid kits, and the posting of occupational health and safety notices. These municipal, structural, and occupational clearances together constitute the required operating permits for the physical office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for the federal Business Number, GST/HST program account and Income Tax Act filings; portal: CRA 'My Business Account' and 'Business Registration Online' (https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/gst-hst.html). Revenu Québec is the competent authority for the Quebec Sales Tax, Quebec corporate income tax and required provincial tax registrations; portal: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/business/.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada or Quebec obtains a federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) with a two-letter GST/HST program account code (typically 'RT') by applying through CRA Business Registration Online, by telephone, or on Form RC1. Once the entity's taxable supplies in Canada exceed the CAD $30,000 small-supplier threshold, GST/HST registration and collection are mandatory. For Quebec, the same entity must register with Revenu Québec for QST using the online registration service or Form LM-1-V, and should obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number from the Registraire des entreprises if the corporation has a Quebec establishment. Supporting documents for a non-resident applicant generally include certified constitutional documents, evidence of the registered office and Canadian representative, list of directors, and a description of the ISIC 6201 vertical CRM cloud software activities. CRA online BN issuance is immediate; Revenu Québec QST account activation may take two to four weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian federal or provincial business corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate taxable entity under Part I of the Income Tax Act; it is not pass-through eligible. A resident corporation is taxed on worldwide income, while a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada is taxed on Canadian-source business income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment, which for Quebec includes allocation to Revenu Québec when the permanent establishment is in Quebec. No tax-exempt zone regime applies to the vertical enterprise software and CRM cloud business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a US-style check-the-box pass-through election; corporate classification follows corporate law and tax residence rules. Relevant statutory elections include (i) a fiscal period election under Income Tax Act subsection 249.1(4); (ii) the closely related corporation election under Excise Tax Act section 156, and the corresponding QST election, to treat intercorporate supplies as made for nil consideration; (iii) voluntary GST/HST and QST registration before threshold; and (iv) treaty-based relief elections available through the competent authority where an entity is treated as resident in both Canada and another jurisdiction. Hybrid mismatch rules apply compulsorily and do not permit elective pass-through recharacterization; no election can make the Inc./Corp. transparent for Canadian corporate tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax), the Canadian federal value-added tax, plus the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), a separate Quebec provincial VAT administered by Revenu Québec. For vertical CRM cloud software supplied in Quebec, the combined headline rate is 14.975%, being 5% federal GST plus 9.975% QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000. Both CRA and Revenu Québec apply the small-supplier threshold based on total worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Once the threshold is crossed, mandatory GST/HST and QST registration applies, and a single taxable supply may itself trigger registration obligations. Voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose continuous transaction controls, real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoice clearance APIs, or digital stamping. GST/HST returns are filed through CRA GST/HST NETFILE or by authorized representatives; QST returns are filed electronically through Revenu Québec's CLICK/online services. Registrants must nevertheless maintain full invoice and transaction records in electronic form, support both B2B and export claims with underlying documentation, and, for Quebec, make business records and invoices available in French.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST and QST registrant may zero-rate (0%) export supplies where (a) goods are exported from Canada in commercial quantities by the supplier or on its behalf, or (b) services, including vertical CRM/SaaS subscription services, are supplied to a non-resident and are not consumed, performed, or exploited in Canada. Cloud CRM subscription fees paid by a non-resident customer located outside Canada are ordinarily zero-rated under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act and the corresponding QST rules, provided the supply is not made to a person in Canada and is not used by a recipient located in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export declaration (Form B13A or Canadian Export Reporting System electronic record), where export reporting is mandatory
Commercial invoice fully describing the goods or services and terms of sale
Bill of lading, air waybill, or motor carrier waybill evidencing physical exportation
Packing list or shipping manifest for goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment/remittance receipt from the non-resident customer
Foreign customs import entry or destination-customs proof of arrival (where obtainable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec treat export zero-rating as high-risk. If the complete export substantiation bundle, including payment evidence and foreign exchange repatriation records, is not available within the expected 180-day examination framework, the zero-rating is reversed and the full combined GST/HST and QST amount is assessed as tax due with retroactive effect plus compound prescribed interest. Penalties under Excise Tax Act section 285 and Quebec's Tax Administration Act include a minimum penalty of $100 plus 25% of the understated tax or overclaimed refund where a knowingly false statement or gross negligence is found, larger penalties for repeat misconduct, and criminal prosecution under section 327 for tax evasion, including fines and imprisonment of up to five years. Erroneous or fraudulent export refunds are clawed back, and director/officer liability can extend to unpaid assessed amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Department of Finance Canada; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating currency regime with no general exchange controls. The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions, including profit remittances, dividends, interest, royalties, and capital repatriation. No Bank of Canada approval or government license is required for foreign direct investment, injection of equity capital, or cross-border borrowing by a Quebec business corporation. Inbound and outbound wire transfers are subject to FINTRAC reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 or more in a single transaction, or twenty-four-hour aggregate), and regulated transactions must comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder will remain subject to Part XIII withholding tax at 25% unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Bank of Canada or any other authorized dealer, no mandatory timeline for the conversion of foreign currency receipts, and no compulsory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain foreign currency in offshore or domestic accounts, use it for operational expenditures, hedge it, or convert it at arm's length market rates. For AML/CFT compliance, export transactions must be supported by commercial documentation such as contracts, bills of lading, customs declarations, and corresponding inbound wires.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with legal constraints. Canada does not recognise the EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) passport; a non-resident EMI cannot directly hold deposits or settle in CAD through Payments Canada systems unless it obtains a Canadian banking licence, becomes a registered federal credit union/trust company, or partners with a Canadian clearing bank as an agent. A pure offshore EMI may be permissible as a treasury visibility account for foreign currency flows but must register as a money services business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA with FINTRAC, enrol with the provincial enterprise registrar in Quebec, and comply with Quebec's consumer protection and payment service rules. Deposit-taking by an unlicensed entity is prohibited under the Bank Act, and capital-protected escrow functions should remain with a prudentially regulated tier-1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is legally permissible under Canadian guidance, and directors are not categorically required to appear physically at a branch. In practice, Quebec banks commonly accept certified corporate records, notarised identity verification, and remotely authenticated director identification if the beneficial ownership structure is transparent and there is a Canadian nexus. A physical or video interview with at least one director or authorised signatory is ordinarily mandatory. If all ultimate beneficial owners are non-resident or the corporation is newly incorporated without prior bank references, banks may require physical presence at a Montreal or Quebec City branch, a notarised attestation, or an in-person visit by a delegated signatory. Compliance documentation should include: Quebec or federal certificate of incorporation, articles and by-laws, registered office address proof, situs of board minutes, director and shareholder registers, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, authorised signing resolutions, proof of address, and government-issued photo ID for all directors and signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner located in a jurisdiction on FATF grey-lists or high-risk non-cooperative lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organisation chart to ultimate individuals; independent source-of-wealth report; source-of-funds documentation with third-party corroboration; tax residence certificates; notarised statutory declarations; a written AML risk assessment; negative media and sanctions screening; explanation of commercial rationale and expected inbound/outbound wire volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face verification of directors or remote incorporation and registered-agent-only substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports or national IDs for each director and significant shareholder; proof of address not more than 90 days old; biometric or liveness-verified video interview records; notarised corporate resolutions; certified English or French translations; evidence of a physical Quebec business address, lease agreement, payroll presence, or contracted management office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-velocity cross-border ERP/CRM receivables without clear matching trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS/vertical ERP contracts with end clients; invoicing and payment acceptance policies; public pricing page; customer onboarding procedures; description of the cloud platform and data processing flows; historical bank statements of the parent; audited or reviewed financial statements; treasury policy describing use of sub-accounts, settlement accounts, and dual-control releases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export control, or restricted-party exposure through an international customer base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Institutional sanctions and export-control compliance policy; automated screening against Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and OFAC SDN List; customer and partner lists with country-by-country exposure; legal opinion on data-centric software classification; contractual anti-sanctions and end-use clauses; proactive disclosure mechanism and a designated AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant share capital or capital escrow amounts arriving from a non-bank finance company, crypto, or unregulated payment intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Originator bank confirmation with SWIFT records; fully identified source of corporate funds; board resolution authorising capital injection; chain-of-title funding ledgers; regulatory or licensing evidence of the originator (bank licence, MSB registration); no-crypto undertaking; completion of FINTRAC large-virtual-currency-transaction reporting if applicable; escrow instructions from legal counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from a foreign parent should be routed as SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 credit transfers with the beneficiary being the Quebec corporation's account at a tier-1 Canadian bank. The transaction must include accurate legal name and Canadian bank transit/branch numbers, a clear remittance information field referring to the share subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement, and the beneficiary address. For balance-of-payments purposes, Canadian banks classify the payment to a business enterprise as a direct investment or intercompany capital transaction; the payer should avoid classifying a true equity injection as a services payment or 'trade settlement'. FINTRAC reporting is triggered on receipts of CAD 10,000 or more, and the bank will validate the corporate existence, the source-of-funds narrative, and if necessary a completed source-of-investment questionnaire. Directors should ensure the underlying transaction is supported by executed corporate resolutions, an updated shareholding register, and either a share certificate or an intercompany loan agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements should occur over a Payments Canada-approved clearing rail. For CAD domestic payments, use Lynx (Canada's high-value real-time gross settlement system) or ACSS for batch items. For cross-border payments, use SWIFT MT103/MT202 and correspond through the tier-1 bank's Canadian clearing branch. Commercial letters of credit should be issued in accordance with UCP600 and, where digital documents are submitted, eUCP; payment is typically effected via SWIFT MT754 and MT799/MT202, with the beneficiary bank receiving through its own clearing membership. The platform should maintain segregated operational and escrow accounts; all disbursements must be matched to a commercial invoice, approved through dual-approval treasury workflows, and recorded with the same reference number in the ERP/CRM cloud ledger to evidence the Value Date, exchange rate, accounting entry, and mirror copy of the settlement confirmation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign exchange forwards for CAD and major convertible currencies
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations or two foreign exchange transactions)
Cross-currency swaps under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex
OTC vanilla foreign exchange options and zero-cost collars
Exchange-traded CAD futures and options on major exchanges such as CME, ICE, or Bourse de Montréal

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where a counterparty cannot legally settle in Canadian dollars due to external exchange restrictions; for a Canadian resident, deliverable CAD forwards are the standard permissible market practice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty; administrative revocation of registration after 3 years of continuous non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee; administrative dissolution order after 2 years of continuous failure to file.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), a reporting issuer is subject to compulsory audit. Non-distributing corporations may dispense with a statutory audit by shareholder resolution where the corporation has no more than 20 shareholders and has not distributed securities. A federally incorporated non-distributing corporation under CBCA may similarly waive the auditor by unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for public enterprises; Canadian private enterprises may apply Canadian ASPE or voluntarily adopt IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Quebec Annual Declaration must include beneficial ownership updates. Share transfers trigger an obligation to amend the internal beneficial ownership register and confirm the updated ownership structure at the next annual filing. Failure to maintain accurate UBO records may lead to penalty and loss of good standing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general rate (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Quebec; 12.2% combined CCPC small-business rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income: 9% federal + 3.2% Quebec)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory sectoral tax holiday; preferential regimes: (i) CCPC small-business deduction lowering combined rate to 12.2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; (ii) federal SR&ED investment tax credit up to 35% refundable for CCPCs and 15% non-refundable for other corporations; (iii) Quebec refundable R&D salary credit up to 30% for SMEs (14% large corporations); (iv) Quebec e-business development tax credit relevant to ERP/CRM software developers; (v) 10% federal provincial abatement on income earned in Quebec
